rationale: Capabilities ['enterprise_wiring', 'caching', 'rate_limiting', 'observability', 'performance'] decomposed from the catalog. Independent work runs in parallel (implement.cache_backend, implement.loadcheck, implement.metrics, implement.rate_limiter); tests and docs branch after implementation and join at review; release waits for review.

One mega implement node: fewer gates, far larger blast radius per failure
outcome: plan with 11 nodes, risk medium

rationale: Read-through cache of the resolved link (positive + short negative TTL): removes the DB from the hot path; negative caching blunts enumeration; Invalidate on PATCH/DELETE: correctness over hit rate for state changes; Per API key for writes, per client IP for redirects: fairness for authenticated clients, abuse protection for public traffic; 429 with Retry-After and X-RateLimit-* headers: standard, client-friendly back-off signal; Per-app CollectorRegistry: isolated in tests, no global state; p95 < 50 ms @ 20 concurrent clients (laptop, SQLite) enforced as a gate: a concrete, repeatable number replaces 'faster'
outcome: design with 4 components, 6 decisions

outcome: +3 nodes, -0, ~4, rerun ['design.enterprise', 'document.enterprise', 'release.readiness', 'test.coverage', 'test.performance']

rationale: Read-through cache of the resolved link (positive + short negative TTL): removes the DB from the hot path; negative caching blunts enumeration; Invalidate on PATCH/DELETE: correctness over hit rate for state changes; Per API key for writes, per client IP for redirects: fairness for authenticated clients, abuse protection for public traffic; 429 with Retry-After and X-RateLimit-* headers: standard, client-friendly back-off signal; Per-app CollectorRegistry: isolated in tests, no global state; p95 < 50 ms @ 20 concurrent clients (laptop, SQLite) enforced as a gate: a concrete, repeatable number replaces 'faster'; Opaque random keys hashed with SHA-256 (keys have 256 bits of entropy, so a slow KDF adds nothing): fast verification on every write without storing secrets; Owner-only PATCH/DELETE: prevents one tenant modifying another tenant's links
outcome: design with 6 components, 8 decisions

rationale: One protocol, two backends: the in-memory LRU keeps the single-process default dependency-free, Redis shares state across replicas. Values are small JSON strings; TTLs are enforced per entry.
alternatives_considered: cachetools TTLCache: rejected, a new dependency for 40 lines of code
outcome: Cache abstraction - bounded in-memory TTL LRU and a Redis backend

rationale: Token buckets allow short bursts while bounding sustained rate. The Redis variant runs the read-modify-write in a Lua script so concurrent replicas cannot double-spend tokens.
alternatives_considered: Fixed-window INCR/EXPIRE: rejected, allows 2x bursts at window edges
Sliding log: rejected, O(requests) memory per key
outcome: Token-bucket rate limiter (in-memory, Redis via atomic Lua) with 429 + Retry-After

rationale: Labels use the route template (/{code}), never the raw path, so cardinality stays bounded. A per-app CollectorRegistry avoids global state and duplicate-registration errors in tests.
alternatives_considered: OpenTelemetry metrics SDK: deferred, Prometheus text is what the platform scrapes
outcome: Prometheus metrics (per-app registry) and ASGI middleware labelled by route template

rationale: Turns "faster" into a measurable, repeatable number. Links are seeded through the service layer, the server runs as a separate process, and each concurrent worker owns its own HTTP connection so the measurement is not dominated by client-side connection-pool contention.
alternatives_considered: In-process ASGI client: rejected, hides network and server overhead
outcome: Load-sanity script measuring redirect p50/p95/p99 against a real uvicorn process

rationale: Additive and reversible. Existing links keep owner_key_id NULL (no owner) so they remain manageable after auth is enabled; new links record the creating key.
alternatives_considered: Backfill an owner for existing links: rejected, no truthful owner exists
outcome: Migration 0003 - api_keys table and links.owner_key_id (FK, SET NULL)

rationale: Redirects resolve through a read-through cache keyed by canonical code (aliases look up their lower-case entry; only canonical misses are negatively cached), invalidated on create/update/delete. Cache errors degrade to the database. Writes and redirects are rate limited per client; readiness now covers the cache; /metrics exposes request, redirect, cache, rate-limit and analytics gauges. Adds redis and prometheus-client as runtime dependencies (approval required).
alternatives_considered: Cache the full Link row: rejected, larger payloads and more invalidation surface
Write-through cache: rejected, invalidation is simpler and links change rarely
outcome: Wire read-through cache, rate limits and metrics into config, app, routes and LinkService

rationale: Opaque 256-bit keys with an indexed prefix, compared in constant time, revocable, never logged. Writes are rate limited per key. Only the creating key may PATCH/DELETE a link (403 otherwise). Redirects, metadata and stats stay public. Existing tests are updated to authenticate.
alternatives_considered: JWT bearer tokens: rejected, needs an issuer and key rotation story for no added value here
bcrypt/argon2 for key hashes: rejected, unnecessary for high-entropy random keys and slow per request
outcome: X-API-Key required on write endpoints; keys SHA-256 hashed at rest; owner-only modification; key CLI

rationale: Attack-oriented tests for the new trust boundary, independent of the implementer's own tests.
alternatives_considered: Rely on the implementer's tests: rejected, separation of duties
outcome: Abuse tests - cross-tenant modification, malformed keys, idempotency scoping, per-key limits, no keys in logs

rationale: API reference and OpenAPI are generated from the running app, so they cannot drift from the code.
outcome: docs for 9 routes; 5 changelog entries
